mika: quick note from today's int6 bring-up: tempesta-v2-compact-int6 failing our multiorient subtitle smoke. two reproducible issues: (A) vertical zh linebreak/punctuation collapsing that shifts subtitle columns, (B) RTL locale bracket/paren orientation flipping in Hebrew samples. attaching short reproducer. :warning:
julia: thanks. can you paste the exact eval command and a tiny failing snippet? keeps things actionable.
mika: command: `rrun eval --model=tempesta-v2-compact-int6 --suite=multiorient_subtitles --shards=small --subset=zh_vertical,hebrew_rtl --concurrency=6`

summary:```
Suite multiorient_subtitles (small)
- zh_vertical: BLEU baseline=30.1 -> tempesta=23.8  (regressions 120/400)
- hebrew_rtl: bracket-orient errors baseline=0 -> tempesta=28/400
- en_subs: unchanged (~0.0 delta)
```

mika: example (zh vertical) input line: 
``
（東京）
``
baseline detok tokens: [（, 東京, ）]
int6 detok tokens:   [（東京）]  # opening bracket glued to ideograph and closing bracket merged -> newline reflow shift

mika: hebrew RTL example: input: שלום (עיר)
baseline decode: same (parens in expected order)
int6 decode: swapped rendering: trailing shows ")עיר(" in visual RTL layout

ken: curious if it's tokenizer merge or decode-time ordering. did the int6 build roll any tokenizer changes?
eli: tokenizer config unchanged. changed bits for int6: per-head quant-scale folding + new kvcache compaction and kernel pack switch to packed-attn-quant. suspect compaction + quant noise alters attention scores; could change marginal decisions in greedy/beam.
hao: ran a quick commit bisect on the build graph. first bad candidate aligns with PR that introduced kvcache compaction heuristics + fold-scale optim.
nobu: could be a post-determinism effect: same token ids but different layout due to bidi shaping code reacting to different unicode joiner insertion decisions. do we observe identical token ids?
mika: I added `--log-token-ids` and `--log-detok` for the failing shard. logs show identical token id sequences across compaction on/off for the Hebrew case, but rendering differs. snippet:
```
case A (compaction ON): token_ids=[12,345,78,901], detok_render=\"... )... (\"
case A (compaction OFF): token_ids=[12,345,78,901], detok_render=\"... (... )\"
```

julia: identical ids but different rendered shapes points to either a runtime bidi/layout pass that depends on intermediate hidden states or an attention-based selection that influences where Joiners are emitted. try `--no-kvcache-compaction --force-stable-quant` to see if that stabilizes.
hao: did that on 200-sample quick run: compaction off + stable-quant reduces zh_vertical regressions from 30%->4% and hebrew flips to 0/200. so compaction seems to amplify quant noise into layout differences.

ken: interesting: if the token ids are identical, then the change is downstream. perhaps we are inserting/removing a ZERO WIDTH JOINER (ZWJ) or mark during detokenization because a hidden-state threshold changed. can we run a per-token hidden-state diff across compaction on/off?
eli: agreed. I ran a short diff on the hidden embeddings for the affected prefix tokens: L2 diff per-token is small but not zero, and attention weight distribution for token index 2 shifts notably when compaction runs earlier. that aligns with compaction merging KVs and causing slight attention redistribution.
mika: I pushed a minimal failing example to the eval bucket at `/evals/smoke/multiorient/zh_he_rtl_flip_1739990001.txt` and added a one-line render png under `/evals/smoke/renders/1739990001/` to help UX see the visual swap.
julia: next steps: 1) add a small smoke test that runs int6 builds with compaction toggled and asserts no bracket orientation flips for RTL locales + no punctuation gastrulation for vertical CJK, 2) gate the aggressive kvcache compaction behind a locale-safe heuristic (detect mixed-direction or ideograph boundary), 3) consider a build flag `--quant-stability-mode` that disables per-head folding for experimental builds. 4) run kernel pack revert (packed-attn-quant -> packed-attn) to confirm.

eli: I reproduced locally with a kernel-only revert: packed-attn (non-quant kernel) keeps outputs stable, packed-attn-quant + compaction triggers failures. opening patch to make compaction conservative on mixed-orient sequences and to add an eval hook.

mika: filing bisect ticket and tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, docs. ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/BR-1248 (brief: int6 kvcache compaction -> multiorient subtitle layout regressions).
sre-bot: canary job queued: tempesta-compact-int6-canary #83002 with compaction=false

julia: thanks all. if someone wants to pair on the hidden-state diff script (ken/hao?), ping me. we'll merge a smoke test first to catch regressions in CI. :rocket:
